newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: BOXING-WOMEN'S FIGHT GAME BACKED BY WBC CHIEF.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-WOMEN'S FIGHT GAME BACKED BY WBC CHIEF.

text.p: World Boxing Council head Jose Suleiman has called for women boxers to be taken seriously -- a view not shared by all the delegates to the council's convention this week.

"We must take female boxing seriously and analyse it," he said in his opening address on Monday. "It seems that women are no longer merely the main sweetness of the world, so we can't close our eyes to women's progress in this sport."
But Argentine WBC member Julio Ernesto Vila countered: "It's madness. Let's see what they do when a woman dies on them in the ring."

One fan in favor is Argentine President Carlos Menem. He welcomed the chance for women to show their fighting skills in public. "Now women are also getting into the ring and showing their courage. Not just in the bosom of the home, where they can get us up against the ropes occasionally," he said.
Women's boxing will be one of the top issues on this week's agenda, along with the dangers of spreading the HIV virus, which can lead to AIDS, in the ring.
The expulsion of boxers from the WBC for fighting in second-rate contests and the creation of an official ranking for referees will also be debated.
